content:
omar.h: Heads up  my March pay included both a UK bonus and a US sign-on adjustment. I moved to London Jan 20 and uploaded my UK tax code on Jan 19. Payslip shows employer taxed the sign-on as US supplemental pay then local PAYE also applied.
lucy.hr: Sorry that happened  can you paste the redacted lines?
omar.h: pasted below
```
Gross sign-on adjustment: GBP 5,000
US supplemental withholding: 22% = GBP 1,100
UK PAYE: 20% = GBP 1,000
Net on slip: GBP 2,900
```
riley.payroll: that looks like our supplemental tax engine applied US rate for the adjustment before the UK residency flag was set. The HRIS -> payroll sync shows an update on Jan 21 but the payroll cutoff for that cycle was Jan 20 17:00 UTC, so it missed the change.
omar.h: So it's our fault? I submitted docs earlier.
lucy.hr: our receipting system shows you uploaded on Jan 19 at 11:02 but HRIS processing was queued; we should have flagged for expedited sync. We'll add that to the postmortem.
tax-bot: Note: treaty credit guidance may apply. Tax team to advise on reclaiming US withholding.
riley.payroll: action plan: create off-cycle to reimburse the US withheld amount net of employer taxes and re-run retro tax in the next UK payroll to adjust PAYE accordingly. Ticket PR-5342 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PR-5342.
omar.h: regex question  what's the timeline to see corrected payslip?
riley.payroll: expect off-cycle posted in 7 business days; corrected payslip and compensation summary added to Self-Service within 10 days.
lucy.hr: apology note sent to Omar via DM. Also adding a step to mark any relocation uploads as "payroll immediate sync" if dated within 5 days of a variable comp run.
omt: closing when resolved.
